body: ports-cleanup-suffixed-run-tags: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ports:run_artifacts (ports:411-439) counts an image as a run's only where its tag matches RUN_TAG '^run-[0-9a-f]{12}$' (ports:75) exactly, or its repository matches COMPOSE_IMAGE '^(run-[0-9a-f]{12})[-_]' (ports:97). An image such as 'vlnab-arch:run-62dc11c74373-amd64' matches neither, so cleanup never lists it. ports --help (ports:62-63) says 'each image tagged with the run tag or named for its compose project'. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: cleanup scans every image docker knows, across every project on the machine, so the match decides what one project's cleanup deletes for all of them; its removed: line counts only the images it found, so a suffixed image stays with no word to the owner. Corpus: decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run says the cleanup 'removes the container artifacts (images, volumes, and networks) of every run tag that holds no lease', and silent on whether a suffixed tag carries the run tag; decision:per-run-artifact-tag and concept:run-tag say a run 'builds every artifact it verifies under that tag', which reads as the tag itself, but neither forbids a suffix; story:verification-leaves-no-artifacts-behind promises 'each verification run's artifacts removed once the run is over'. Harm: a run that builds under a suffixed tag (an architecture suffix, as the driver's machine held 28 images of another project, e.g. 'gridiq-allinone:run-d61aae7a593d-amd64', 6.24GB) fills the disk the story promises to keep clear; A9 arguably covers the removed: line only if it claimed the run clean, and it counts what it removed. Options: (A) exact match: the decision says a run's image carries the run tag exactly, and the rules layer (cheatsheet's per-run section) tells the owner to tag images with the run tag alone; cost: suffixed builds leak until removed by hand, and the owner learns only from the rules text. (B) prefix match: any image tag that begins with the run tag followed by '-' or '_' is the run's; cost: one project's cleanup deletes other projects' suffixed images after the hour of grace, a widening of what decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run already accepts for exact tags. (C, the filer missed it) keep the exact match and have cleanup print a line naming each image whose tag carries a run tag with a suffix and left in place; cost: one more output line, the disk still fills until someone acts, and the decision still needs a sentence saying suffixed tags stay. Each option amends decision:run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run. Sibling issues: none open.

certification-cannot-land-its-own-delta: Evidence, re-verified: the sprint alignment pass compares each delta with its artifact byte for byte (C3) (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/sprint-pass.md:25). converge/SKILL.md:In sprint mode (SKILL.md:103) applies the ownership test 'even where the sprint's change edited the file or a delta names the artifact: a fix in the corpus or the harness settings sets the item to judgment', and converge/prompts/merge.md:The ownership test (merge.md:34) sends a 'corpus' file to judgment with no fix round. Contract item 1 at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:244 reads 'Every corpus matches every delta above, applied verbatim', and the goal rule (sprint-document.md:262-263) exempts only 'A stuck defect listed in the return'. The filed problem still holds at this tree. Mechanism: a judgment item is not stuck, so an unlanded delta leaves item 1 unmet and outside the exemption; a goal checker then either loops on a sprint nobody in the run may finish, or ignores item 1. Corpus: decision:runs-fix-what-the-project-owns leaves 'the design corpus and the coding standards, which change only through a sprint's deltas' alone and sends 'A defect whose fix lies in the corpus' to the intake as a judgment issue; decision:sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository says 'The goal is met when the contract's items verify there' and exempts only a stuck defect; concept:corpus-delta says 'Verification that deltas were applied verbatim belongs to the completion contract and to sprint certification', which names verifying, not landing; story:certify-completion promises 'done' means the same thing for every sprint. Harm: A9, a goal checker reports not done (or done over an unmet item 1), and the contract has no outcome a run can reach. Options: (A) certification lands its own sprint's approved delta verbatim: amend decision:runs-fix-what-the-project-owns so landing the sprint's own delta is a change through that sprint's deltas; cost: a run edits the corpus, which the decision now reserves to execution, and the converge skill, merge prompt, and ownership test need a sprint-delta exception. (B) the goal rule exempts a judgment item certification lists for the owner, as it exempts a stuck defect: amend decision:sprint-goal-read-from-the-repository; cost: a sprint whose approved corpus change never landed reads as done, so item 1 is no longer a term the goal holds. (C, the filer missed it) certification hands an unlanded delta back to sprint execution (a build task re-filed against the sprint) before it returns, so the executor that owns applying deltas lands it; cost: certification no longer ends on its own terms, and the converge skill gains a step that reopens execution. Sibling: sprint-contract-stuck-check-two-verdicts (now a defect on the same goal rule's stuck-check verdict); rule this before its fixer rewrites the goal rule, or alongside it.

discover-design-back-edge-kinds: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md:Phase 2 Reviewer Prompt (SKILL.md:520-546) asks for a request only where thin material 'blocks a sharper concept', with heading '### <affected-concept-slug>', field '- Missing: <one sentence stating what the concept can't currently say>' and field '- Promote new concept: <name | none>'. The Back-Edge Extractor Prompt (SKILL.md:657-690) expects a request that 'names the affected artifact kind and slug', edits 'a story's Story statement; a decision's Choice, Rationale, or Alternatives', and promotes only where the request authorized 'Promote new artifact'. The skill's overview (SKILL.md:40) says the back-edge re-discovers 'areas the phase 2 reviewer named as too thin, then re-extraction and re-review of the affected artifacts only', naming no kind. The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: the orchestrator fills the extractor's requests from the reviewer's block (SKILL.md:58-60), so a concept request and a concept promotion reach the extractor; the extractor's story and decision branches are never fed. Corpus: story:bootstrap-design-corpus promises 'the as-is design model extracted autonomously into durable catalogs plus a queue of judgment questions' and is silent on the back-edge and its kinds; no decision names the back-edge. Harm: no accept-list entry covers it as a defect: no wrong result, crash, or lost data; a thin story or decision stays thin and its gap may surface as an issue instead of a sharper artifact. Options: (A) concepts alone: cut the extractor's story and decision branches and rename 'Promote new artifact' to 'Promote new concept', a skill-text change; the story may stay silent or say so; cost: a thin story or decision gets no second read, only an issue. (B) every kind: the reviewer names the kind in each request ('### <kind>:<slug>', 'Promote new artifact'), and its inclusion test covers stories and decisions; cost: a larger back-edge and a reviewer prompt that judges thinness for three kinds. The filer's options both amend story:bootstrap-design-corpus; either choice can land as skill text alone, since the story's promise holds under both, so whether the story records the scope is part of the owner's choice. Sibling issues: none open.
